xcode.name: Xcode
xcode.derived_data.title: Derived Data
xcode.derived_data.what: Build products, indexes and intermediate files that Xcode keeps for every project you have opened.
xcode.derived_data.why: Xcode recreates everything here on the next build. Your code and project settings are not stored in this folder.
xcode.derived_data.after: The next build and indexing of each project will take longer than usual.
xcode.archives.title: Archives
xcode.archives.what: Builds made with Product › Archive, together with their debug symbols (dSYM).
xcode.archives.why: Old archives are only needed to symbolicate crash reports or to upload that exact build again.
xcode.archives.after: Crash reports from deleted builds can no longer be symbolicated on this Mac. Keep archives of versions that are still live in the App Store.
xcode.device_support.title: Device support files
xcode.device_support.what: Debug symbols copied from an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch for every OS version you have connected.
xcode.device_support.why: Xcode copies them again the next time you connect a device with that OS version.
xcode.device_support.after: The first connection of such a device takes a few minutes while symbols are copied.
xcode.documentation.title: Documentation cache
xcode.documentation.what: Developer documentation that Xcode downloaded and indexed.
xcode.documentation.why: Xcode downloads and indexes the documentation again when you open it.
xcode.documentation.after: The first documentation search will be slower.
xcode.previews.title: SwiftUI previews
xcode.previews.what: Builds and simulator data used to render SwiftUI previews.
xcode.previews.why: Xcode rebuilds a preview when you open it.
xcode.previews.after: The first preview of each view will take longer.
